Folks — initial tri-region tiling proposal based on Nebula workbook + typical L70B-like throughput. High-level assumptions (please verify with Nebula):
- Avg seq len: 256 tokens for generation, 64 tokens for control/embeddings
- Avg tokens per query: 320 weighted across flows
- Target ramp: week0=10% traffic, week2=40%, week4=100%
- Model deploy: single replica family (70B fp16/4-bit quantization candidate) with KV cache enabled

Proposal (sizing = H100 equiv nodes, rounded):
- US (primary routing + burst): 14 H100 nodes (estimated sustained capacity ~480 rps generation equivalent, includes 15% buffer). Host as routed-hosted with pinned reserved tranche of 8 nodes, burst to shared pool for spikes.
- EU (data-resident + predictable): 9 H100 nodes (sustained ~300 rps gen). Recommend dedicated pool (reserved) to satisfy residency and predictability.
- APAC (Singapore, latency-sensitive): 7 H100 nodes + 4 smaller 80GB A100-like nodes for edge microbursts (steady state ~260 rps gen). Dedicated pool recommended for APAC pilot.

Buffering & SLA notes:
- Keep 10–20% headroom above forecast for week4 growth and variance.
- Canary strategy: start with 30% traffic to US pool pinned set, 20% to EU, 10% to APAC in week1 then shift per ramp schedule.

Cost & procurement (very rough):
- Reserved monthly commit (all regions): estimated $170k–$240k/month depending on exact node SKU and quantization.
- Activation lead time for dedicated pools: 3–5 weeks for US/EU, 4–6 weeks for APAC (Singapore) depending on quota and partner infra.

Operational runbook bullets (for Priyom to expand):
- Pin model version and use canary route policy; automatic fallback to smaller quantized variant on overload.
- Enable prefix/KV caching for session reuse; cache warmup plan during canary.
- Tracking: add per-route token cost dashboard and latency SLO alerts; predefine rollback thresholds.

Attachments I will produce: tiling_proposal_qtr4.csv (node-by-node breakdown) and a short SOW sketch. Please review and I will iterate.

Karthik
Sr. Product Manager, Capacity Planning
